pr.title: Make jump threading state sparse
pr.description:
Continuation of https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/127024

Both dataflow const-prop and jump threading involve cloning the state vector a lot. This PR replaces the data structure by a sparse vector, considering:
- that jump threading state is typically very sparse (at most 1 or 2 set entries);
- that dataflow const-prop is disabled by default;
- that place/value map is very eager, and prone to creating an overly large state.

The first commit is shared with the previous PR to avoid needless conflicts.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The supplied PR is a performance-only data-representation change: JumpThreading/ValueAnalysis moves from a dense bottom-filled IndexVec to a sparse FxHashMap with a documented invariant that absent keys mean BOTTOM and inserting BOTTOM erases a key. The historical material contains no regression-test hunk, no changed MIR input/output expectation, and no documented wrong jump-thread transformation or miscompile. The changed all()/all_bottom() Unreachable behavior is also not shown to be reachable from TOFinder::is_empty or to produce a wrong program result. Therefore any "original vs transformed" pair would have to invent a bug (e.g., deliberately making missing keys mean TOP or retaining BOTTOM entries), which is not the historical incorrect transformation justified by this PR. No source-grounded counterexample can be validated.

analysis.summary: JumpThreading/ValueAnalysis state was changed from a dense bottom-filled IndexVec to a sparse FxHashMap that stores only non-bottom ConditionSet values. The reusable correctness rule is that every sparse operation must preserve the dense lattice semantics: an absent key means bottom, inserting bottom must erase the key, and join must treat absent entries as bottom. This is a performance optimization, not a confirmed jump-threading miscompile fix; the patch also changes the Unreachable behavior of the old all() helper to all_bottom() and supplies no regression-test hunk.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, ValueAnalysisWrapper::State stored StateData::Reachable(IndexVec<ValueIndex, V>) sized to the place/value map and filled with V::BOTTOM; ConditionSet::default() was the empty condition slice. State::all scanned every dense entry and returned true for StateData::Unreachable. Jump threading created State::new(ConditionSet::default(), self.map) and flooded with ConditionSet::default().
analysis.incorrectTransformation: No wrong MIR rewrite or miscompile is documented by this PR. Historically the dense state representation was semantically correct but expensive because it cloned a full vector even though jump-threading state usually has only a few non-bottom entries. The optimization changes the state representation only; it is not evidence of a historical incorrect jump-thread transformation. Sparse code becomes incorrect if it treats an absent key as unknown/absent instead of bottom, retains keys whose value became bottom, or performs join/all_bottom over the wrong set of entries.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by JumpThreading through ValueAnalysis state, especially bodies whose tracked discriminant/local ConditionSet entries are mostly bottom and where a tracked local is overwritten or flooded before a control-flow join. The domain includes reachable states with an empty sparse map, reachable states with one or two non-bottom ConditionSet entries, and the distinct State::Unreachable state.
analysis.trigger: Use sparse state storage when JumpThreading/ValueAnalysis repeatedly clones or joins a large eager place/value map but only a small number of ConditionSet entries are non-bottom. The sparse map is also exercised when a previously non-bottom condition is overwritten/flooded to ConditionSet::BOTTOM before a branch or join.
preconditions: ConditionSet must satisfy HasBottom with BOTTOM equal to the empty condition slice and is_bottom matching that empty slice.
StateData must store only values that are not bottom, as stated by the map invariant.
Reading a missing ValueIndex must return the state's bottom value rather than failing or returning top.
Inserting a bottom value must remove the map entry; inserting a non-bottom value must store it.
Join must iterate the other state's non-bottom entries and treat a missing entry in self as bottom, while a missing entry in other contributes no change.
State::Unreachable must remain distinct from State::Reachable with an empty or all-bottom map; callers using all_bottom must justify how they handle the changed Unreachable result.
clone_from must copy the sparse map completely enough that no stale entries survive and no required non-bottom entries are lost.
pitfalls: Assuming a missing map key means 'unknown' or top would change jump-threading decisions; the patch defines it as bottom.
Keeping a bottom value in the map breaks the stated invariant and can make later joins/scans behave differently from the dense representation.
When joining sparse states, an entry present only in the other state must be inserted as a non-bottom contribution; entries absent from the other state must not erase or top-initialize self.

The helper semantics changed: old all() returned true for StateData::Unreachable, while new all_bottom() returns false for State::Unreachable. If an unreachable state can reach TOFinder::is_empty, the result is not equivalent to the old dense helper.
ConditionSet::default() was replaced by ConditionSet::BOTTOM in flood operations; these must denote the same empty condition set.
A test that only starts from an empty state will not catch failure to erase bottom entries; clearing, flooding, and joining previously non-bottom entries are the important cases.
The supplied patch contains no regression-test hunk, so sparse-state invariants and the Unreachable/all_bottom behavior are not directly covered by new tests in this diff.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused Rust unit tests around the sparse State/StateData behavior: (1) get on a missing index returns BOTTOM; (2) insert(non-bottom) then insert(BOTTOM) removes the entry and get returns BOTTOM; (3) joining a state missing a key with another state containing a non-bottom value inserts it and reports changed; (4) joining a bottom-free state with another state containing only bottom or no entries reports unchanged; (5) all_bottom is tested for reachable empty, reachable with a non-bottom condition, reachable with a map entry equal to bottom (invariant violation), and Unreachable. Add a JumpThreading mir-opt regression case where a tracked condition is established, then flooded/overwritten before a branch or join, and assert the threading output matches the dense behavior; also include a case that can exercise an unreachable state if the caller permits one. No test hunk is present in the supplied patch, so these tests would need to be added rather than inferred from existing changes.
